plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like composite flower heads made of golden ray florets surrounding a dark central disc. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is grown both as an ornamental and as a major oil and seed crop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North America, Europe, Ukraine, Russia and Argentina (native to North America)
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds exhibit heliotropism, following the sun from east to west each day, but mature blooms stop moving and face east, which helps warm them and attract more pollinators.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms dense colonies and produces arching plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It is a vital late-season nectar and pollen source for bees, butterflies and other insects preparing for autumn.
plants.location: Meadows, roadsides and prairies of North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like goblet flowers in early autumn, before its leaves emerge. The leaves appear the following spring and die back by summer, so the flowers rise on bare ground.
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges of Europe, from the UK to central Europe; cultivated worldwide in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that has been used medicinally for gout and is also used by plant breeders to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, made of a central cluster of tiny flowers surrounded by large, stiff, colorful bracts. It grows in the fynbos vegetation of the Cape region and is South Africa's national flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak bloom from about late August to November
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The genus is named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change shape, referring to the great diversity of forms in the protea family, which is more than 80 million years old.
